Incident Type: FIXED
Material: JET FUEL: JP-8
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: MINOT AIR FORCE BASE
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 48.420000, -101.353611 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 450 gallon
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** DURING THE DAILY INSPECTION IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT HYDRANT PIT #11 CONTAINED A LARGE AMOUNT OF A FUEL/WATER MIXTURE WITH NO APPARENT SIGNS OF A LEAK. THE SYSTEM WAS NOT BEING USED AT THE TIME AND WAS NOT PRESSURIZED. 600 GALLONS OF THE FUEL/WATER MIXTURE WAS REMOVED. AFTER REMOVAL IT WAS ESTIMATED THAT THERE WERE 450 GALLONS OF JP8 IN THE MIXTURE. ONCE THE FUEL/WATER MIXTURE WAS REMOVED IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE LOW POINT DRAIN VALVE WAS PARTIALLY OPEN AND THE CAP WAS OFF. THE VALVE AND CAP HAVE BEEN SECURED AND COORDINATION HAS BEEN MADE TO PRESSURE TEST THE PIT.

Report DescriptionBLUF: WASHINGTON STATE FERRY (WSF) CATHLAMET ALLIDED WITH A DOLPHIN (PIER DOCKING STRUCTURE), RESULTING IN SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE TO THE VESSEL. NO INJURIES TO PASSENGERS OR CREW. DETAILS: SECTOR PUGET SOUND (SPS) RECEIVED A REPORT FROM SEATTLE PD AND THE WSF OPCEN OF AN ALLISION BETWEEN FERRY CATHLAMET AND A DOLPHIN AT THE FAUNTLEROY TERMINAL (SW SEATTLE) RESULTING IN SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE TO THE PORT SIDE OF THE SUPERSTRUCTURE. SEATTLE FD/PD ARRIVED ON SCENE AND DETERMINED THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE PASSENGERS OR CREW. SPS COMMAND CENTER CONFIRMED WITH WSF CAPTAIN ABOARD THE VESSEL. ALL PASSENGERS WERE EVACUATED FROM THE VESSEL, AND VEHICLES REMOVED AFTER SUCCESSFUL DOCKING AT THE FAUNTLEROY TERMINAL. 02 VEHICLES ON THE PORT SIDE REMAIN PINNED BY THE DAMAGED SUPERSTRUCTURE OF THE VESSEL. ALLISON WAS ABOVE THE WATERLINE, AND THERE IS NO POLLUTION AT THIS TIME. DOLPHIN IS ALSO SIGNIFICANTLY DAMAGED. FERRY REMAINS DOCKED AT THE FAUNTLEROY TERMINAL. CURRENT ESTIMATES ARE $500,000 OR GREATER IN DAMAGE ACCORDING TO THE PORT CAPTAIN FROM WSF, MEETING THRESHOLD FOR MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY. CASE PENDS.

SORBENT PADS WERE DEPLOYED TO THE VESSEL AND WATERWAY. THERE IS CURRENTLY NO VISIBLE SHEEN IN THE WATERWAY. IT WAS ADDITIONALLY NOTED THE REFUELING STATION AND THE VESSEL HAD APPROPRIATE REMEDIATION EQUIPMENT TO HANDLE THE DISCHARGE.
